request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person row now shows a settled-total and an open-total, and the sheet shows both totals under the table. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it's worked out:** a person's claims that count are split by status.
- **Settled-total:** the dues of their SETTLED claims, at their frozen figures. A correction is counted the same way, under whatever status it has.
- **Open-total:** the dues of their OPEN and PENDING claims. Held, deferred and retired-and-excluded claims are left out, because the check that decides this is the same one the due-total uses.

Each claim's due comes from the same calculation the due-total already uses. So the two figures always add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the cap. The sheet's two figures are everyone's added up, without leaving out the highest and lowest.

**Where it lives:** the whole change is in the front end, in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. The app already works out the due-total on the screen, and the spec expects no new audit lines, so I didn't touch the server or the database.

**When the due-total shows n/a:** a claim with no due counts as 0, so the person shows numbers rather than n/a in both new columns. The spec doesn't test that case.
